dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1797 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 240 items printed somewhere; by the finder's count 3 reach 5 papers, 29 reach 4, 140 reach 3). The same script was run with year 1796 over the 1797 pages (items_from_1796.json: 49 items, 13 in 4 papers, all parts of one publication of January). Every item in 4 or more papers was read, the items in 2 or 3 papers were checked automatically for a further paper by a wider text match, and the counts were checked item by item with phrase searches over all 1,587 pages of 1797 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json); every hit was read. AI review on the session's own model; not an independent human review.
dispositions.selection_rule: Adopted for 1797 on 23 November 2026, on the review's recommendation, which the owner asked it to follow: a story needs one single printed item in 4 or more papers, because only 8 series survive for 1797 (three all year, 2 to 6 in print in any three weeks), so no item reaches 7 papers, or 6; 1793 uses 6 for the same reason. Every single item in 5 papers was admitted, except digests; items in 4 papers were chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news: every document, letter or report in 4 papers was chosen, and single paragraphs of London, Paris and Hamburg news columns, verse, an anecdote and a printer's notice were not. Items are counted by their own words; a printing counts where its opening survives; two printed forms of one report are counted together, as 1809 counted two translations of one bulletin. A sub-story could have fewer papers under a parent that reaches the threshold; this round has none. The 21 stories of rounds one and two stay as they are; this round adds groups beside them.

deferred_addition.S97-034: The New Hampshire Gazette, 13 December 1797, page 2: Adams's reply of 29 November to the House, a printing of the round-two group congress-opening-nov-1797 that round two missed. counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted item by item, two single items of 1797 reach 5 papers: the Tenerife report (a story of round one) and the Vienna report of 26 July (in two printed forms, 3 + 2 papers). Twenty-five reach 4: the eight stories admitted here; seven stories of rounds one and two (Adams's farewell address, the paragraph on Andrew Brown's death, Blount's letter, the Algerine battle, the brig Brothers, the Hermione 'Particulars' and Duncan's Camperdown dispatch); and ten items read and not admitted (below). Everything else read is in 3 papers or fewer.
counted_item_by_item.Joins made by the finder: The finder joins items that were printed together in one run of news. The run of Paris news of early November 1796 that four papers printed (Gazette of the United States 9 January, Patowmac Guardian 19 January, Republican Gazetteer 24 January, Kentucky Gazette 8 March) holds Truguet's letter, Bournonville's letter and the Paris paragraph on the Dey of Algiers, each in those 4 papers, and other paragraphs in 1 to 3. The London news of late August 1797 joins the Brussels paragraph on the definitive treaty and the paragraph on dispatches from Scotland, each in 4 papers. Each was counted by its own words.
counted_item_by_item.Openings that do not survive: The President's message of 19 January 1797 with the Secretary of State's letter to Mr. Pinckney was printed in instalments. Its opening survives in 3 papers (Gazette of the United States, New Hampshire Gazette, Patowmac Guardian); the Virginia Argus of 14 February and the Republican Gazetteer of 28 February hold only its continuation, their earlier issues being lost. By the rule other years used (a printing counts where its opening survives; 1809 dropped such a page), it is in 3 papers.
counted_item_by_item.Pages that only quote an item: Not counted: the Gazette of the United States of 5 June, which quotes Adams's speech of 16 May; the Secretary of State's letter to the Spanish minister of 8 August, which quotes the 'western letter' on the Spanish posts; a New Hampshire Gazette digest of 22 November that rewords the Hague paragraph of 19 September.
counted_item_by_item.A printing missed by round two: Adams's reply of 29 November 1797 to the House of Representatives is also on page 2 of the New Hampshire Gazette of 13 December; that issue's RevX transcriptions are filed one page off, so round two's phrase searches missed it. With it the reply is in 4 papers. Decided 23 November 2026 to add it; deferred to a correction release (see deferred_addition).

stories_of_rounds_one_and_two.reach the 1797 threshold (4 papers by on: Eight: the Tenerife report (5), Duncan's Camperdown dispatches (4), the Algerine-Sicilian battle (4), the Hermione 'Particulars' (4), the brig Brothers (4), Adams's farewell address (4), Blount's letter (4), and the paragraph on Andrew Brown's death (4). A ninth, Adams's reply to the House of November 1797, reaches 4 once the deferred printing is added.
stories_of_rounds_one_and_two.kept below the threshold: Thirteen as admitted (twelve once the deferred printing is added), kept as reviewed stories though no item of theirs reaches 4 papers: the opening of Congress of November 1797 (3 per item until then), Boyd / Bantry coverage (3), Barney escapes the blockade (3), Sonthonax leaves Saint-Domingue (3), Quito earthquake (3), Peace / Cayenne context (2), Peace and Plenty boarding (3), Two Sisters wreck (two texts, 1 paper each), French captures at Havana (3), Special session of Congress (3 per item, 5 papers across its parts), Kosciuszko's land warrant (3), Jefferson's letter to Madison (3), New Hampshire governor's address (3). Decided 23 November 2026 (the owner asked the review to follow its recommendations): kept, because they were read and checked against their scans before the rule, the Boyd story is the pilot that the release's consumer view and checks are built on, and treating them as not admitted would need a correction release and changes to the site for no gain in accuracy. Recorded as an exception for the full audit (docs/rules-and-exceptions.md).

points.1 threshold: Adopted: 4 papers for 1797 (as 1793 uses 6), because only 3 papers survive all year and 2 to 6 are in print in any three weeks.
points.2 stories of 6 November: Kept: the 13 below the threshold (12 once the deferred printing is in) stay reviewed, recorded as an exception; 8 reach it.
points.3 Vienna report in two forms: Counted together (5 papers), as 1809 counted two translations of one bulletin.
points.4 the letter to Mr. Pinckney: Not admitted: its opening survives in 3 papers; continuation pages do not count, as in 1809.
points.5 items that are not news: Not chosen: a song, an anecdote, a printer's notice; listed as read and not admitted.
points.6 a paragraph on one man: Not admitted: it turns on one man and would add a second Blount story; described without his name.
points.7 single news-column paragraphs: Not chosen, as 1793 and 1809 did; their months are covered.
points.8 the printing round two missed: Decided to add; deferred to a correction release, because a ledger cannot change an existing group's topic row (add_reviewed_topics.py reproduces existing rows exactly). Checked and cropped: outputs/story_discovery_1797/round3/deferred/.
points.9 the not-admitted list: Round three's entries go into work/not_admitted.json when the ledger is applied (reapply_not_admitted.py), so the published list and the site change together.
